messages:
jo: Noticed partner requests being billed to wrong project during midnight spike. billing-alert from finance at 02:45 UTC. anyone oncall?

maya: looking at logs, many requests have header X-Redwood-Origin but routed_project shows fallback. sample: `auth=ok header=partn-a claims= - routed=fallback-project`.

kevin: suspicious. we deployed parallel auth validators last week; possible race where routing uses first available claim (token) and misses header enrichment.

ops-bot: alert: billing-attribution-anomaly threshold breached (10m >2%). Paging eng-platform.

jo: quick mitigation options: 1) make header enrichment synchronous for now, 2) change unattributed default to shared-billing-temp, 3) prefer header if present (for partner keys only), 4) fail ambiguous requests.

maya: prefer 2 short-term + canary 1 to measure latency. changing default avoids immediate customer charge.

kevin: I'll push a canary to reorder middleware (header injector before token parser) and run tests. also add `auth.attribution_source` metric with values header/claims/fallback.

deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-middleware v1.9.3-canary -> 10% traffic. CI green.

ops-bot: sampling bumped to 100% for attribution traces for 10m.

jo: canary results after 6m: fallback routing down from 3.4% -> 0.4%. latency p95 unchanged. promoting to 50%.

maya: opening telemetry PR and a small console banner in Keys that flags keys with any fallback-billed activity in last 24h.

kevin: follow-ups: unit test for middleware ordering, telemetry + dashboard, partner outreach for refunds if >$100. closing incident after monitoring window.

ops-bot: incident mitigated. summary: middleware reorder canary fixed attribution race; default pool set to shared-billing-temp during roll.
